description: Jebadiah LoRA sweep on one rented NVIDIA GPU box: public data only, one run at a time, most informative first. v1 adds two runs on data-v1 (HelpSteer2 train and SummEval added to the pool).
estimate_basis: ESTIMATES, not measurements. Scaled from v0: Qwen3.5-4B-Base, 1 epoch over 11,391 questions (2.87 M prompt tokens) took 2 h 19 min of training on a GB10 (a DGX Spark shared with another engine, cuBLAS running sm80 kernels on sm121 at about 7 to 11 TFLOPS effective). Assumed training speedups over that box: H100 PCIe 80 GB x12, A100 80 GB SXM4 x7 (the loop is small-batch and launch-bound, so far below the FLOP ratio). 9B costs 2.25x the 4B per token. Eval is 17,000 scored questions per run at batch 16 (H100 about 10 min for the 4B, 18 for the 9B; A100 x1.7). Model load and temperature fit add about 3 min. sweep-status.json carries the measured minutes; the first run is the real calibration of these numbers.

defaults.effective_batch_note: v0 trained batch 2 x accumulation 4 = 8 examples per optimizer step; the 80 GB box takes the same 8 in one micro-batch, so the step count and the schedule are v0's.

headline.definition: macro accuracy (repeat 0, in percent) over the zero-shot public sets: jevals-pubmedqa, jevals-banking77, jevals-helpsteer2, nimble-eval, kev-transfer-v4__test, and the macro over the nimble-public__* subsets counted as one component. typed-decisions-test and kev-decision-v7__test share datasets with the pool and are reported beside it, not in it.

runs.name: smoke
runs.purpose: 12 optimizer steps on the 4B, an 8-record eval of every set and a temperature fit: proves the environment, the data and every stage before the paid runs. A failure here stops the sweep.

runs.name: 9b-v0
runs.purpose: Qwen3.5-9B-Base with the exact v0 recipe: the biggest expected gain (Nimble's number lives at 9B).

runs.name: 4b-2ep
runs.purpose: 4B, v0 recipe, 2 epochs: does the one-epoch run under-fit?

runs.name: 4b-scorefix
runs.purpose: 4B, v0 recipe plus the score-type calibration fix: score questions train towards a unimodal ordinal kernel around the hard label (adjacent level 0.2 of the label's weight) instead of the teacher's spread, and the score temperature is fitted against that same target (held-out training loss) instead of the argmax label. v0's score T of 0.39 came from fitting hard labels to a model trained on soft ones; it sharpened HelpSteer2 into ECE 0.385.

runs.name: 4b-v0
runs.purpose: 4B, v0 recipe replicated on this box (same kernels, fp32 read): the anchor every 4B delta is measured against, and the r16 side of (d) when 1e-4 is the better learning rate.

runs.name: 4b-lr2e-4
runs.purpose: 4B, v0 recipe at lr 2e-4: the learning-rate probe that decides which lr the rank comparison runs at.

runs.name: 4b-r32
runs.purpose: 4B rank 32 (alpha 64) at the better of the two learning rates by headline; compared with the r16 run at that lr.

runs.name: 9b-best
runs.purpose: 9B with the best 4B change (the candidate whose headline beats 4b-v0 by the most); skipped when no candidate beats the anchor.
runs.est_note: about 75 / 130 min if the winning change is 2 epochs

runs.name: 9b-base-eval
runs.purpose: Qwen3.5-9B-Base with no adapter on the same sets (the base row of the 9B card). Optional, cheapest, last.

runs.name: 9b-v1
runs.purpose: Qwen3.5-9B-Base on the v1 pool (the v0 pool plus HelpSteer2 train and SummEval score questions), score_targets ordinal and the temperature fitted on the training target, exactly as 4b-scorefix. Trains on data-v1; the eval sets stay the v0 ones under data/test.
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split (15,813 pool questions, 44.8 percent of them score): 1.9 s per step measured on the 9B is 59 min, plus 26 min of eval. SummEval prompts carry a whole article, so the step time can run above the v0 mix's 1.9 s.

runs.name: 4b-v1
runs.purpose: Qwen3.5-4B-Base on the v1 pool (the v0 pool plus HelpSteer2 train and SummEval score questions), score_targets ordinal and the temperature fitted on the training target, exactly as 4b-scorefix. Trains on data-v1; the eval sets stay the v0 ones under data/test.
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split: 1.7 s per step measured on the 4B is 53 min, plus 23 min of eval. Same caveat on the SummEval prompt length as 9b-v1.

runs.name: 4b-v1-lr2e-4
runs.purpose: learning-rate probe on the v1 recipe (lr 2e-4 vs 1e-4)
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split: 1.7 s per step measured on the 4B is 53 min, plus 23 min of eval. Same caveat on the SummEval prompt length as 9b-v1.

runs.name: 4b-v1-r32
runs.purpose: rank probe on the v1 recipe (r32/alpha64 vs r16/alpha32)
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split: 1.7 s per step measured on the 4B is 53 min, plus 23 min of eval. Same caveat on the SummEval prompt length as 9b-v1.

runs.name: 9b-v2
runs.purpose: 9B on the v2 pool (30.5k questions, 23 percent score), one epoch, score fix
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split (15,813 pool questions, 44.8 percent of them score): 1.9 s per step measured on the 9B is 59 min, plus 26 min of eval. SummEval prompts carry a whole article, so the step time can run above the v0 mix's 1.9 s.

runs.name: 4b-v2
runs.purpose: 4B on the v2 pool
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split: 1.7 s per step measured on the 4B is 53 min, plus 23 min of eval. Same caveat on the SummEval prompt length as 9b-v1.

runs.name: 4b-v2-r32
runs.purpose: 4B on the v2 pool at rank 32
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split: 1.7 s per step measured on the 4B is 53 min, plus 23 min of eval. Same caveat on the SummEval prompt length as 9b-v1.

runs.name: 4b-v2-cn
runs.purpose: 4B on choice and noul only (split-adapter experiment, half one)
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split: 1.7 s per step measured on the 4B is 53 min, plus 23 min of eval. Same caveat on the SummEval prompt length as 9b-v1.

runs.name: 4b-v2-score
runs.purpose: 4B on score only (split-adapter experiment, half two)
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split: 1.7 s per step measured on the 4B is 53 min, plus 23 min of eval. Same caveat on the SummEval prompt length as 9b-v1.

runs.name: 9b-v2b
runs.purpose: 9B on the filtered v2 pool: synthetic families with teacher agreement >= 0.82, synthetic noul capped at 3,000, score back near 27 percent
runs.est_note: about 1,860 optimizer steps at batch 8 over the 14,900 questions of data-v1's train split (15,813 pool questions, 44.8 percent of them score): 1.9 s per step measured on the 9B is 59 min, plus 26 min of eval. SummEval prompts carry a whole article, so the step time can run above the v0 mix's 1.9 s.

runs.name: 4b-c20
runs.purpose: 4B on data-dose-c20: the v1 pool unchanged plus 3,984 synthetic CHOICE questions (165 to 168 per family, whole states, no synthetic noul), 20.1 percent of a 19,797-question pool. The dose question: does a fifth of synthetic choice keep v2's choice gains without v2's loss on the six human yes/no sets? Read against 4b-v1 (headline 70.34, six-set pooled 83.23).
runs.est_note: 2,340 optimizer steps at batch 8 over 18,713 train questions (1,862 v1 steps + 478 synthetic). At the brief's flat 1.7 s per step: 66 min training, 92 min total with 23 min eval and 3 min temperatures/load. At 2.3 s: 90 / 116 min. On the measured 4b-v1 rate (3.20 s per v1 step, 5,953 s for 1,862 steps) plus 1.60 s per synthetic step (9b-v2 minus 9b-v1, scaled by the measured 4B/9B ratio 0.858): 112 / 139 min. The estimate field uses the measured figure.

runs.name: 4b-c33
runs.purpose: 4B on data-dose-c33: the v1 pool plus every synthetic choice question (7,858), no synthetic noul; 33.2 percent of a 23,671-question pool. The top of the dose curve, and exactly data-v2 minus its 6,856 synthetic noul questions, so it is the first run with synthetic choice and zero synthetic noul.
runs.est_note: 2,800 steps over 22,398 train questions (1,862 v1 + 938 synthetic). 1.7 s: 79 min training, 105 total. 2.3 s: 107 / 133. Measured rates: 124 / 152.

runs.name: 4b-c10
runs.purpose: 4B on data-dose-c10: v1 pool plus 1,795 synthetic choice questions (74 to 76 per family), 10.2 percent. The low point of the dose curve; run only if 4b-c20 beats 4b-v1 on the headline and the curve shape matters.
runs.est_note: 2,078 steps over 16,619 train questions (1,862 v1 + 216 synthetic). 1.7 s: 59 / 85 min. 2.3 s: 80 / 106. Measured rates: 105 / 132.

runs.name: 9b-c20
runs.purpose: 9B on data-dose-c20, launched with --only after the 4B readout, and only if 4b-c20 (or 4b-c33) passes the gate in yesno-data/REPORT.md: headline at least 4b-v1's 70.34, and pooled accuracy on the six human yes/no sets no more than 1.0 point under 4b-v1's 83.23.
runs.est_note: 2,340 steps: 1,862 v1 steps at the measured 3.73 s (9b-v1, 6,938 s) plus 478 synthetic steps at 1.86 s (9b-v2 minus 9b-v1): 130 min training, 25 min eval, 3 min temperatures and load.

runs.name: 4b-c20h
runs.purpose: 4B on data-dose-c20h: data-dose-c20 plus 3,000 HUMAN-labelled noul questions (CondaQA 1,000, ContractNLI 1,000, ShARC 1,000; converter and pool built 2026-09-24, see workers-2026-09-24/human-noul/REPORT.md; lint ok, eval-overlap check dropped the one BoolQ passage leak). The replacement test: does human noul recover or add to the yes/no sets where teacher noul did not? ShARC's license is unclear (CC BY-SA 3.0 tag only), so this pool is for internal research runs; anything that ships trains on 4b-c20h-alt.
runs.est_note: 2,696 steps (21,562 train questions / 8; c20's 18,713 plus 2,849 human noul). At the rented H100 PCIe rate measured on 4b-c20 on 2026-09-24 (about 4.2 s per step) that is about 190 min of training plus about 27 min eval; the 153 min figure assumed the earlier 1.7 to 2.3 s rates.

runs.name: 4b-c20h-alt
runs.purpose: 4B on data-dose-c20h-alt: the same as 4b-c20h with LexGLUE UNFAIR-ToS (CC BY 4.0) in place of ShARC. Every source here has an explicit license (CondaQA Apache-2.0, ContractNLI CC BY 4.0, UNFAIR-ToS CC BY 4.0), so this is the pool for a version that ships.
runs.est_note: 2,696 steps (21,563 train questions / 8). Same timing as 4b-c20h.

runs.name: 4b-v3-c20f
runs.purpose: 4B on c20 with the synthetic choice targets swapped from the DeepSeek+Qwen average to Fable 5.1 (same states, same questions). Read against 4b-c20 (71.56): how much of the choice gain was lost to label noise.
runs.est_note: Same recipe as 4b-c20 (rank 16, lr 1e-4, one epoch, ordinal score targets, temperature fit on train); only the labels or the added questions differ.

runs.name: 4b-v3-c20f-n3k
runs.purpose: 4B on data-v3-c20f plus up to 3,000 Fable-labelled synthetic yes/no questions on the same states. Read against 4b-v3-c20f: does yes/no from a good teacher help or still hurt the six human yes/no sets.
runs.est_note: Same recipe as 4b-c20 (rank 16, lr 1e-4, one epoch, ordinal score targets, temperature fit on train); only the labels or the added questions differ.

runs.name: 4b-v3-c20fh-alt
runs.purpose: 4B on data-v3-c20f plus the 3,000 human-labelled yes/no questions (CondaQA, ContractNLI, UNFAIR-ToS). Read against 4b-v3-c20f and 4b-c20h-alt.
runs.est_note: Same recipe as 4b-c20 (rank 16, lr 1e-4, one epoch, ordinal score targets, temperature fit on train); only the labels or the added questions differ.

runs.name: 9b-v3
runs.purpose: 9B on the full v3 recipe (v1 pool + Fable-labelled synthetic choice at the c20 dose + 3,000 public human yes/no + 54 Prolific splits). The candidate for the published 9B v2. Read against 9B v1 (73.3) and v2 (72.2).
runs.est_note: Same recipe as 4b-c20 (rank 16, lr 1e-4, one epoch, ordinal score targets, temperature fit on train); only the labels or the added questions differ.

runs.name: 4b-v3-full
runs.purpose: 4B on everything human we have: v1 pool + the c20 dose of synthetic choice with Fable 5.1 targets + 3,000 public human-labelled yes/no (CondaQA, ContractNLI, UNFAIR-ToS) + 54 Prolific human splits (round 1, readers only, agreeing families). Read against 4b-c20 (71.56). Trains on a Spark, not a rented box.
runs.est_note: Same recipe as 4b-c20 (rank 16, lr 1e-4, one epoch, ordinal score targets, temperature fit on train); only the labels or the added questions differ.

runs.name: 9b-v3s
runs.purpose: 9B on data-v3-full with the two public score sets (HelpSteer2 train, SummEval train) duplicated, restoring the score share that v1 had; the answer to v3 losing 6 points on HelpSteer2 while gaining on choice and yes/no.
runs.est_note: Same recipe as 4b-c20 (rank 16, lr 1e-4, one epoch, ordinal score targets, temperature fit on train); only the labels or the added questions differ.

runs.name: 4b-chat-v1
runs.purpose: The v1 recipe on the CHAT model Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B (thinking off) instead of the Base: the single biggest recipe difference between Jebadiah and the JPT models that lead the Decision Index. Read against 4b-v1 (70.34).
runs.est_note: Same steps as 4b-v1 (about 1,880). The chat checkpoint is the vision-language layout; if the trainer cannot load it as a causal LM the run fails at load and that is the finding.

runs.name: 9b-chat-v1
runs.purpose: The v1 recipe on the CHAT checkpoint Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B (thinking off). 4b-chat-v1 scored 72.49 (best 4B ever, +2.2 over 4b-v1) with no synthetic data, so the base checkpoint is the lever. Read against 9b-v1 (73.29): the candidate for the published 9B v2.
runs.est_note: Same steps as 9b-v1 (about 1,880); on the A100 about 100 min training plus 30 min eval.

totals.note: H100 PCIe total about 4.4 h including the smoke and the optional base eval, inside the 5 h budget with the stated assumptions; A100 about 7.4 h.
totals.v1_note: 9b-v1 and 4b-v1 are the v1 data runs, launched on their own with --only 9b-v1,4b-v1; they are not in the totals above, which cover the v0-data sweep.
